title: Fix dead cues.emotion field lookup and add multi-dimensional affect matching in memory retrieval

sections.what: Fix the broken `player.emotion.label` vs `player.emotion.current` field mismatch in `memory-context.ts` that zeroes out emotional memory recall in live runs, and upgrade `engine/memory_retrieval.py` Channel 4 from a single scalar label to multi-dimensional and target-bound affect matching.
sections.why: `engine/serialization.py` serializes `player.emotion.current` and the 35-dimension `player.emotions` map, whereas `memory-context.ts` reads `player?.emotion?.label || player?.current_emotion || ''`, sending empty cues to `/memories/retrieve` so Channel 4 scores 0.0. Furthermore, crisis scenes evoke overlapping emotions simultaneously (e.g. terrified, guilty, protective/affectionate, angry) that a single scalar label flattens away.
sections.how: 1. Fix `static/js/agent/prompt-builder/memory-context.ts` to read `player?.emotion?.current` (keeping `.label` as legacy fallback) and forward active above-baseline affect entries from `player.emotions` (computed via `engine/emotion.py`) along with dominant intensity (`0..1` normalized cleanly against retrieval expectations).\n2. Extend `engine/memory_retrieval.py` (`extract_cues` and Channel 4 `score_memory`) to accept multi-dimensional `emotions` maps/lists alongside legacy scalar `emotion`, weighting congruency across co-occurring dimensions (`afraid`, `guilty`, `anxious`, `angry`, `affectionate`, etc.) and relational `who`/`why` targets stored in `memory.emotions`.
sections.verify: 1. Run pytest retrieval tests confirming mixed-emotion states (`afraid` + `guilty` + `affectionate`) score non-zero Channel 4 matches on both `emotion.current` and secondary dimensions.\n2. Run JS unit tests asserting `PromptBuilder.buildMemoryContext` emits `player.emotion.current` and active `player.emotions` dimensions in `retrievePlayerMemories` payloads, then run `npm run build:ts`.

acceptance.text: `static/js/agent/prompt-builder/memory-context.ts` reads `player?.emotion?.current` (plus `player?.emotions` active map), fixing the silent `""` miss caused by reading nonexistent `emotion.label` / `current_emotion`.

`cues` sent to `/memories/retrieve` includes top deviant active dimensions from `player.emotions` (from `engine/emotion.py`) and optional relational affect (`who` / `why`) instead of collapsing mixed states to one scalar word.

`engine/memory_retrieval.py` Channel 4 (`Emotional Congruency`) scores multi-dimensional affect overlap and target-bound (`who`) emotion similarity against stored `emotion` and `memory_emotions` vectors.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Agent Lens (`static/js/agent-lens.ts`) retrieval breakdown and Character Inspector Mind/Emotions display.

Current availability: `engine/serialization.py` publishes `player.emotion.current` and `player.emotions`, while `memory-context.ts` reads `player?.emotion?.label || player?.current_emotion` (returning empty string in live sessions).

Why no standalone UI change needed: Fixes broken cue extraction between `/api/state` and `/memories/retrieve`; reflected directly in Agent Lens emotional channel scoring.

Manual verification steps:
1. Trigger a mixed high-stakes state (e.g. `afraid`, `guilty`, `affectionate` toward another character elevated simultaneously in `player.emotions`).
2. Inspect the `POST /api/players/<id>/memories/retrieve` request payload and `explain: true` breakdown in DevTools / Agent Lens.
   - expected: Request sends non-empty primary emotion plus active `emotions` map, and Channel 4 (`emotional`) scores non-zero matches across co-occurring affect dimensions.
